- The verdict bands are the shared helper's: `|gap| < 2%` = `no_move`, a sign flip = `reverse`, the move given back = `faded`, otherwise `held`.
- **A gap that HELD INTO THE BELL is the signal at this slot; a gap that faded is not.**
- **The halt state is not measurable this session** — the TradingView scanner's `halted` column is null on every row, so no halt count is published anywhere in this digest.

---

**The headline**

- **The inflation print broke the relief bid, and the tradeable board got rebuilt from scratch underneath it.** The **October CPI came in hot** —
- headline **+0.4% m/m** against a +0.3% consensus and core **+0.3%** against +0.2%, and because last year's shutdown left the bureau with no October 2025 base, **no year-over-year figure was published at all**.
- The 10-year yield jumped to **4.983%** (from 4.864%), the two-year surged about 19bp to **4.74%**, and Fed Governor Christopher Waller —
- who said *before* the release that a hot print should put a **50bp hike** "on the table" — is now backed by the data:
- CME FedWatch moved to roughly **85% odds of a 25bp hike and 15% of 50bp** for December 8–9, up from 84% priced on Monday.
- The market gave back about half of Monday's rally:
- the **S&P 500 settled -0.38% at 7,520.93**, the **Nasdaq Composite -0.74% at 25,065.88**, the **Dow -0.30% at 52,231.89** and the **Russell 2000 -0.71% at 2,820.55**.

- **The caveat that changes how this should be read: the headline index understated the damage.** The **equal-weighted S&P was down only about 0.2%** while the cap-weighted index fell 0.38% —
- the selling was concentrated in the mega-caps, and **Nvidia alone is the story**.
- The Information reported that CEO **Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang facilitated the shipment of at least $7.5bn of chips through Chinese firms**, on top of the board's independent investigation and the FBI inquiry the President confirmed;
- **NVDA closed -5.53% on $71.03bn of turnover** (RVol 2.43), took out the $170 level chart watchers had flagged, and is on track for its **lowest close since March 30**, with an RSI of 23 —
- the most oversold reading since June 2019 — with **earnings next Tuesday**. **Chip stocks have now lost roughly $5trn of market value since October 6**,
- about a quarter of their worth, while the typical S&P 500 stock is up about 4% over the same stretch.
- The **equal-weight line and the cap-weight line disagree, and that disagreement is the day's real finding.**

- **The third thing worth saying is that the tradeable end of the board is company-specific and mostly idiosyncratic —
- and it is split hard by sign.** The **single-stock winners are earnings-and-clinical stories**:
- **PEPG +92.89%** on Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 data showing **46.5% mean splicing correction, the highest reported in a multiple-dose study**;
- **TTEC +72.04%** on a Q3 beat, a reaffirmed FY26 outlook and a 10-Q that flags a possible sale of its Digital business; **ZIP +53.15%** on a Q3 beat-and-raise;
- **AAON +19.31%** on a record quarter that raised FY26 sales growth to 72–75%. The **losers are guidance and capital-structure events, not a macro read-through**:
- **HIMS -16.56%** on a double miss and an EBITDA cut, **APPS -35.84%** on four points of gross-margin compression despite a revenue beat, **GRPN -23.05%** on a guidance cut, **PAYS -18.94%** after a 10-Q disclosed the loss of 113 plasma centers, **MNTK -57.19%** because it cannot file its 10-Q on time, and **BMGL -64.26%** on a Nasdaq volatility pause over a dilutive offering.
- **The AI-power complex is the one place where macro and company met**:
- **GEV -3.92%** after SoftBank disclosed a **$3.73bn loss** on slot fees for US AI data-centre equipment, and the gap **faded** from -8.90% at the open to -3.89% at the bell.
- **At this slot the gap that held is the signal, and 416 of 943 names held into the bell.**

**Method and caveats**

- **Every published price and volume is the SETTLED 2026-11-10 regular-session close and the settled regular-session volume.** The close is the bridge's `market-recap` post-bell regular-session print, cross-checked against the Nasdaq official quote API's post-bell `secondaryData` field;
- the volume is the bridge's settled session volume. Nothing on this board is a live intraday print.
- **One source per field.** Where the Nasdaq official close and the bridge close disagreed by more than 0.6% (13 names:
- BWET, CTEV, HYLN, SSK, GDMN, AZUL, NEHI, MTA, GCTS, NEWP, XTND, COOK, SJT), the **bridge was published** because Yahoo's own daily bar corroborated it on all 13 and contradicted the Nasdaq `secondaryData`.
- The change percentage is recomputed from the **same** source's close and previous close, so no row mixes a close from one source with a percentage from another.
- **RVol = settled session volume ÷ the trailing-10 settled average from the same series** (the 10 sessions ending 2026-11-09, market-wide from `polygon-io grouped_daily`, 12,006 symbols with a complete denominator).
- The screener's own RVol column uses a different denominator and is **not** mixed in.
- **The gap verdicts are computed at the bell, not at 15:50.** The shared helper's `now` column prefers the 15:50 bar;
- at the pre-close slot the question is whether a gap *held into the bell*, so the annex verdicts were recomputed at the **16:00 close** from the same Yahoo 5-minute series.
- The bands are the helper's: `|gap| < 2%` = `no_move`, a sign flip = `reverse`, the move given back = `faded`, otherwise `held`.
- **The halt state is not measurable this session** — the TradingView scanner's `halted` column is null on every row. No halt count is published anywhere in this digest.
- (BMGL's mid-session **volatility trading pause** is a price-action event reported by the issuer's data feeds, not a halt count derived from the scanner.)
- **The board is wide by construction and the tradeable end is thin.** 943 names cleared the floors, of which **16 are Tier A and 2 Soft-A**.
- The 138 TECH_WATCH and 785 Tier B names are the *beta*, not stories — they are published so the imbalance is visible, not because they are tradeable.
- **The counts in the tier headings are the full tier counts; the tables are capped.**
- **Every row carries its catalyst provenance.** `has_catalyst_timestamp` is `yes` where the catalyst carried a verified timestamp and `no` where it did not, and `reason_without_timestamp` carries the **reason** on every one of the 943 rows —
- including the explicit "no same-session company catalyst located" for the names where a search was run and found nothing.
- A blank reason would read like "nothing happened" when in fact the reason exists and was simply never timestamped.
- **Buyout / near-offer rule applied.** No name on this board was promoted on a deal announcement alone. **TTEC** is the closest call:
- the 2024 $6.85 non-binding take-private proposal was **withdrawn on 2025-07-31** and the special committee was dissolved on 2025-08-15, so today's +72.04% is **not** that spread —
- it is the Q3 beat plus the 10-Q's flagging of a possible sale of the Digital business.
- It trades far below the old proposal price and the move is a genuine re-rating, not an arb.
- **Low float is flagged, not used to demote.** **STAK** (+20.17% on $79m) has no same-session company catalyst located —
- the most recent company news is a 2026-11-05 non-binding LOI worth "hundreds of thousands of dollars" — and it is treated as a low-float squeeze, not a catalyst name.
- **BMGL** and **XGN** carry the dilution flags that keep them out of the momentum tier.
- **The macro read is a rate read, not a growth read.** The hot CPI lifted the 10-year to 4.983% and the 2-year about 19bp, and **XLF (+0.50%) was the best of the 11 sectors** while tech was the worst —
- the market bid the rate-sensitive complex and sold the long-duration one. That is why the equal-weighted S&P (about -0.2%) barely moved while the cap-weighted index fell 0.38%.
- **Two names lack a bridge session volume** (**BH.A** and **LEN.B** — class-share tickers the bridge does not carry) and are published with their price and RVol from the other sources;
- their RVol is computed on the scanner volume rather than the bridge volume, and the CSV records the price source used.
- **The Nasdaq sweep priced 895 of 943 names**; the bridge priced all 943. Both are settled 16:00 closes, and the disagreement set is disclosed above rather than silently resolved.
